author: Tomás Grüner
subject: feat(storage): diff beacon states against their snapshot, not their parent (#684)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Stacked on #683.

Today a beacon non-anchor state is stored as an xdelta3 delta against
its **parent**. A cold read of a state late in an epoch therefore folds
up to 31 deltas in sequence, each over a full encoded state. This PR
diffs every non-anchor beacon state against the **nearest snapshot on
its branch** instead, so a cold read is one snapshot plus one delta.

## What Changed

- **Writer** (`state_writer.rs`): the writer's memo changes from the
parent's encoded bytes (`encoded_memo`, `encoded_parent_bytes`) to the
current snapshot's bytes (`snapshot_memo`). A new `last_base` records
which snapshot the last written state belongs to.
- **Common case:** the parent is the state written just before, so
finding the base needs no read.
- **Miss** (a restart, or a fork off an older block):
`nearest_snapshot_root` follows `StateDiffs` frames to the first root
with no diff row. On a beacon directory a state is a snapshot or a diff,
never both. It never probes `States` with `contains`, since on RocksDB
that reads the whole blob value.
- **`plan_beacon_state_write`:** the frame now names the snapshot as its
`base_root`. `StateWrite.encoded` is `Some` only for snapshots.
- **Reader:** unchanged.
- **Docs:**
- the state writer module doc, `insert_state`, `beacon_state_delta.rs`
and the `StateDiffs` table doc;
- `BEACON_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL` / `snapshot_interval`, which now explain
that the interval bounds delta size and snapshot frequency rather than
the length of the fold (the value is unchanged);
  - `docs/data_storage.md`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- **No `DB_VERSION` bump:** every frame names its own base, so a
directory holding parent-linked diffs from an earlier build still reads.
The writer's walk also handles such rows when picking the snapshot for a
new diff.
- **One writer thread is still required:** a diff's snapshot must be
committed before the diff is planned, and the reader's walks rely on the
commit order.
- **Lean is unchanged:** its `StateDiff` rebuilds
`historical_block_hashes` from the parent link, which only holds when
the base is the parent.
- **Trade-off:** a diff now carries every change since its snapshot, so
diffs grow through the epoch. The total size of an epoch's diffs grows
roughly with the square of the number of slots instead of linearly. My
estimate from the measured ≈270 KiB per-slot diff is up to about the
size of a snapshot per epoch. That estimate is unmeasured. With #683's
pruning, only the last few epochs are kept, which is why this PR is
stacked on it.

## Tests Added / Run

- **Added in `store.rs`:**
  - `every_beacon_diff_in_an_interval_names_the_intervals_snapshot`
- `two_children_of_a_mid_interval_block_both_diff_against_the_snapshot`
- `a_restart_mid_interval_keeps_diffing_against_the_snapshot`: exercises
the memo miss.
- `the_snapshot_walk_follows_old_parent_linked_rows_to_the_snapshot`:
uses hand-written parent-linked rows.
- **Updated:**
- `a_cold_beacon_state_reads_back_as_its_snapshot_plus_one_delta`,
renamed from the old fold test;
  - the `plan_beacon_state_write` unit tests in `state_writer.rs`.
- **Lib tests passing** (`--profile release-fast --lib`):
  - `ethlambda-storage`: 162
  - `ethlambda-state-transition`: 325
- `make lint` is clean.
- **Not run locally:** spec-test suites, and a measurement of real diff
sizes on a mainnet follower.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Based on #683 (finalized state pruning).

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt`: clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`): clean
- [ ] Ran `make test`: lib tests of the affected crates only; spec
suites not run locally

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: perf(beacon): write epoch balances through an in-order copy-on-write cursor (#647)
body:
## Motivation

An epoch boundary writes every balance. `get_mut` on a tree list buffers
a copy of each element in a dense map, sorts the map into a second
`Vec`, then rebuilds every touched leaf and recomputes the root of every
written element, changed or not. The altair rewards step calls it up to
eight times per validator (four reward/penalty pairs, each as increase
then decrease), and `process_effective_balance_updates` reads
`balances()[i]` per validator, which was only cheap because the rewards
pass had just filled the map.

This PR adds an in-order lazy copy-on-write write cursor to
`ethlambda-ssz-tree` and moves the epoch balance writes onto it.
Expected gain (estimate, not measured on a real chain): tens of ms off
each epoch-start block at mainnet registry size. The import-replay
benchmark was not run for this PR.

## Changes

| commit | what |
|---|---|
| `perf(ssz-tree): add an in-order copy-on-write write cursor` |
`List`/`Vector::iter_cow`, `IterCow::next_cow`, `ElemCow::{index,
make_mut, set}`, `try_update_each`; `with_updated_leaves` generalized
over a leaf source; unit tests and model-based property tests |
| `perf(beacon): apply epoch balance and effective-balance writes
through the cursor` | `BeaconState::registry_mut` (disjoint borrows of
validators and balances); `apply_balance_deltas` used by the altair+ and
phase0 `process_rewards_and_penalties`; both
`process_effective_balance_updates`; new `tree_bench` rows; docs |

How the cursor works: it walks leaves in order and copies a leaf on the
first write that reaches it. At the leaf's end it compares only the
touched offsets with the original; if all are equal, the original leaf
(its `Arc` and cached hash) is kept. Otherwise the new leaf carries over
the element roots of unchanged elements and computes the changed ones.
On drop, one descent swaps the changed leaves in and rebuilds only their
paths. Pending buffered writes are applied before the pass starts.

## Design decisions

- `Drop` does the work, and the tree is untouched during the pass, so an
early return or a panic leaves a consistent list holding the writes so
far (tested with `catch_unwind`).
- Names as in the design: `iter_cow`, `next_cow`, `make_mut`, `set`,
`try_update_each`. No `set_with`.
- Changed composite elements get their root computed eagerly, on the
state-transition thread.
- A kept `Arc` or carried root always follows an actual comparison. The
cursor only creates fresh empty hash cells, or carried roots for a leaf
it owns; it never fills a shared `OnceLock`.
- Spec order for balances: per index, each pair is
`saturating_add(reward)` then `saturating_sub(penalty)`, pairs in order.
Deltas are never netted. Each balance depends only on its own deltas, so
index-by-index equals the spec's pair-by-pair loop.
- `apply_balance_deltas` lives in `helpers/mutators.rs` and is shared by
the phase0 and altair+ paths. It keeps the old error for a balances list
shorter than the registry, and does not touch balances past the registry
length.
- Rewards and both effective-balance passes move together: once rewards
bypass the map, the effective-balance reads would otherwise become tree
descents.
- Effective-balance updates only copy a leaf when the new effective
balance differs from the old one (it can equal it when capped at the
maximum).
- No leaf-slice API, no parallel bulk update.

## Not in this PR

- Switching `Balances` to a sparse `BTreeMap` update map: to be decided
after measuring whether a dense writer remains.
- `List::filled`: its only consumer is the participation-list work,
which is deferred.
- Migrating slashings, inactivity, and registry updates: sparse, flat
lists, or part of the epoch single-pass rewrite (#630, #632, #633).
Expect a merge conflict with #632 in `process_rewards_and_penalties`.
- Import-replay benchmark and any remote profiling.

## Testing

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p ethlambda-ssz-tree --profile release-fast` | 71 unit +
31 model tests passed (before the second commit) |
| `cargo test -p ethlambda-types --profile release-fast --lib` | 197
passed |
| `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --profile release-fast
--lib` | 324 passed, 16 ignored |
| beacon spec suite, mainnet preset, full | 5734 passed, 4 failed |
| beacon spec suite, minimal preset, full | 40038 passed, 4 failed |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --profile
release-fast -- -D warnings` and the state-transition
`beacon-spec-tests` variant | clean |
| `cargo check -p ethlambda --profile release-fast` | ok |

The 4 spec failures in each preset are the `gossip/*` suites
(`gossip_beacon_block`, `gossip_data_column_sidecar`,
`gossip_beacon_aggregate_and_proof`, `gossip_beacon_attestation`): the
local gossip fixture directory is intentionally empty, so they match no
cases. Every other suite, including `epoch_processing`, `rewards`,
`sanity`, `finality`, `random` and `transition`, passes.

### tree_bench (2.4M validators, `--ignored`, single run)

Noisy: run while the machine was under a load average above 100 from
other builds, so absolute numbers (and even the order of the old rows)
are unreliable; read them as rough ratios only.

| row | ms |
|---|---|
| `epoch_sweep_tree` (old path) | 333.8 |
| `epoch_sweep_tree_phases` | write 58.1, apply 70.0, hash 83.1 |
| `epoch_sweep_cursor_tree` | 26.8 |
| `epoch_sweep_noop_cursor_tree` | 90.4 |
| `epoch_sweep_rebuild_tree` (rebuild baseline) | 105.8 |
| `rewards_apply_4_pairs_get_mut` | 342.5 |
| `rewards_apply_4_pairs_cursor` | 158.9 |
| `eb_updates_indexed` | 253.8 |
| `eb_updates_cursor` | 115.4 |
| `lockstep_three_lists_cursor` | 136.2 |

The bench asserts the cursor rows produce the same roots as the old
paths, and that a no-op sweep keeps the tree (`ptr_eq`).

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: perf(beacon): cache the total active balance per epoch (#648)
body:
## Motivation

`get_total_active_balance` rescans the registry about ten times per
ordinary block: once per attestation (through
`get_base_reward_per_increment`), twice in the sync aggregate, plus
churn and fork-choice callers. Each call built an index `Vec` of the
active validators and then read every index back with a `validator(i)`
tree descent. In the profile taken for the persistent-tree registry
change, this was the largest cost left after hashing (the plan's
estimate: about 414 ms per block at mainnet scale; an estimate, not
measured here).

## Changes

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `perf(beacon): sum the total active balance in one registry pass` |
`get_total_active_balance` is one in-order `validators().iter()` pass
with the same `saturating_add` and one-increment floor as
`get_total_balance`. No index `Vec`, no descents. Every caller gets it,
cached or not. Randomized test (inline SplitMix64) against
`get_total_balance(get_active_validator_indices(..))`, plus an all-zero
registry. |
| `perf(beacon): cache the total active balance per epoch in the store`
| New `ActiveBalanceCache` (`ethlambda-storage`), held by the `Store`
beside the committee cache (`Store::active_balance_cache()`). Key
derivation and lookup in `ActiveBalanceCacheExt`
(`helpers/accessors.rs`). Attestation processing (altair, deneb,
electra) and `process_sync_aggregate` take it; plumbed up through block
processing and `state_transition`. New metric
`lean_beacon_total_active_balance_lookups_total{result}`. Docs in
`beacon_stf.md` and `metrics.md`. |
| `perf(beacon): read each attester's validator once per attestation` |
The effective balance is read once per attester, lazily on the first
newly earned flag, instead of once per flag. |

## Design decisions

- **External cache, not a state field.** The design review chose a
store-held table like `CommitteeCache` over a non-SSZ cache field on
`BeaconState`. That keeps the state type, its SSZ derive and its fork
upgrades untouched: no libssz change, no `rebase_on` adoption, no reset
at upgrades.
- **Why the key is sound.** The total for a state in epoch E is fixed by
two inputs. Effective balances are written only by epoch E-1's
`process_effective_balance_updates`; the Electra upgrade zeroes only
never-activated validators, which are not active at E. The active set at
E cannot change inside E, because every activation and exit lands at
least `MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD` epochs ahead; deposits append validators that
are not yet active; slashing sets `slashed` but leaves effective
balances alone (the spec's total keeps slashed validators). So `(E,
block root at the last slot of E-1)` identifies the history: two states
agreeing on it agree on the total. Sibling branches that diverge during
E-1 have different roots, so they get different entries.
- **Decision root differs from the shuffling key.** The shuffling key
uses the last slot of E-2, since the seed is fixed ahead of use; the
total is not, so it needs the later root. A new key type
(`ActiveBalanceKey`) keeps the two apart.
- **Epoch 0** keys on the genesis block root (slot 0), like the
shuffling key does for its first epochs. A state that cannot name the
root (the genesis state itself, or a root outside the history window) is
`unkeyable`: computed, not cached.
- **Only block processing uses the cache.** Between
`process_effective_balance_updates` and the slot increment a state is in
epoch E-1 but already carries E's balances, so a key rooted at the end
of E-2 would be wrong there. Block processing never runs in that window
(`process_slots` has already advanced the state), and epoch processing
keeps the uncached one-pass function. Documented on
`active_balance_key`.
- **Debug cross-check.** Every hit is compared against a fresh
computation under `debug_assert_eq!`, so a missed writer fails the
fixtures (`release-fast` keeps debug assertions on).
- **No single-flight.** A concurrent double compute on a miss is
accepted: the value is one cheap registry pass and both callers compute
the same number.
- **`on_block` reads the store's cache itself**
(`store.active_balance_cache()`), so its signature and the chain actor
are unchanged. Other callers (spec runners, block production, unit
tests) pass `ActiveBalanceCache::default()`.
- **Capacity** is a small constant with eviction of the lowest epoch;
entries are tiny, so room for several forks is cheap.
- **Per-attester read stays lazy** so that an attester earning no flag
is still never read, which keeps error behavior identical.

## Not in this PR

- Fork choice's `get_proposer_score` and `calculate_committee_fraction`
keep calling the uncached function; another change replaces that total
with a justified-balances snapshot.
- Epoch processing and the pulled-up tip: they compute totals inside the
single-pass epoch summary work (#630, #632, #633).
- Churn helpers (exits, consolidations, slashings): rare per block, they
use the one-pass function.
- A flat effective-balance epoch cache (progressive balances): waits
until something consumes it.

## Testing

Measured on release-fast with debug assertions. The import-replay
benchmark was not run for this PR, so there is no measured speedup to
report.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --profile
release-fast -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p ethlambda-state-transition ... --features
beacon-spec-tests -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test -p ethlambda-storage --lib` | 142 passed, 1 ignored (run
before the store-sharing test was added; not re-run after) |
| `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --lib` | 330 passed, 16
ignored |
| beacon spec suite, mainnet (full) | 5734 passed, 152 ignored, 4 failed
|
| beacon spec suite, minimal (full) | 40038 passed, 3692 ignored, 4
failed |
| `cargo check -p ethlambda --profile release-fast` | clean |

The 4 failures per preset are the gossip `matched_fixture_cases` checks:
the gossip fixture tree is empty in this environment, so they match no
cases. Every other suite passes.

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: chore(beacon): refresh Sepolia's config from eth-clients (#693)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Our built-in Sepolia config is `eth-clients/sepolia`'s
`metadata/config.yaml` byte for byte, but two upstream changes since the
copy had not been picked up:

-
[eth-clients/sepolia#130](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/130):
schedule a 200M gas limit at the Glamsterdam upgrade.
-
[eth-clients/sepolia#120](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/120):
set the `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH` override Sepolia's merge used.

## What Changed

`bin/ethlambda/assets/sepolia/config.yaml` is copied again from
`eth-clients/sepolia` at `7b1b9d9` (`main` today; the file last changed
in `ddd2eb06`):

| Key | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH` | `0x00…00` | `0xd07cce97…a37bc1` |
| `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH_ACTIVATION_EPOCH` | `18446744073709551615` |
`3599` |
| `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` | absent | 200M gas at epoch `353024`
(`GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH`) |

`bin/ethlambda/src/main.rs`: the comment on `first_config_difference`'s
transition group said every shipped network leaves these keys at their
defaults, which Sepolia no longer does. It now gives the reason they are
left out regardless.

`bootstrap_nodes.yaml` already matches upstream.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH` + activation epoch | Only `validate_merge_block`
reads them, and only for the merge transition block, which Sepolia
passed in 2022. `/eth/v1/config/spec` now reports the published override
instead of the zero hash |
| `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` | Not a `Config` field, so it is listed in the
ignored-keys warning at startup, next to the Gloas keys already there |

Existing Sepolia data directories still resume:
`first_config_difference` leaves the transition keys out, and a resume
that passes writes the file's config over the stored one
(`Store::replace_config`).

## Tests Added / Run

No new tests: nothing pins Sepolia's transition keys.

```bash
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo test -p ethlambda --profile release-fast --bins
```

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [ ] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — not run; the only
Rust change is a comment
- [ ] Ran `make test` — ran `cargo test -p ethlambda --profile
release-fast --bins` only, which holds the network/config tests

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(beacon): read SLOT_DURATION_MS when a network config omits SECONDS_PER_SLOT (#691)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`ethlambda beacon --network <dir>` ignored a config's
`SLOT_DURATION_MS`. `derive_genesis_fields` always set `slot_duration_ms
= seconds_per_slot * 1000`, and `Config`'s container-level serde
`default` fills a missing `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` with mainnet's 12.

The `config.yaml` that kurtosis' ethereum-package generates
(ethereum-genesis-generator v6.2.7) carries only `SLOT_DURATION_MS`,
since consensus-specs dropped `SECONDS_PER_SLOT`. So any kurtosis devnet
with `seconds_per_slot != 12` ran ethlambda on a 12-second clock with no
error.

## What Changed

The slot-time rule now lives in one place, `reconcile_slot_time` in
`network/config_file.rs`, called from `ConfigFile::parse`. Built-in
networks and loaded directories both parse through it. It reads the raw
key set to tell an absent key from one holding the default:

| Keys in the file | Behavior |
|---|---|
| both | `SECONDS_PER_SLOT * 1000` must equal `SLOT_DURATION_MS`;
otherwise startup fails naming both keys and values |
| only `SLOT_DURATION_MS` | must be a non-zero whole number of seconds;
`seconds_per_slot` is derived from it |
| only `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` | `slot_duration_ms` derived from it (as
before) |
| neither | mainnet defaults (as before) |

- `network/mod.rs`: `derive_genesis_fields` now only sets

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(beacon): cache the anchor's execution hash so its child imports optimistically (#710)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

A checkpoint-synced `ethlambda beacon` paired with an execution client
that is still syncing sat at its anchor for up to ~25 minutes, logging
`Not importing: the execution client has not validated this block and it
is not an optimistic candidate` for the first post-anchor block until it
was 128 slots old. Found by ethrex's multisync (lambdaclass/ethrex#7461)
on Hoodi: ethlambda parked ~11 minutes and failed the run's 10-minute
head-stall check, while Lighthouse in the same setup imports
immediately.

It is a spec deviation. `specs/bellatrix/optimistic-sync.md`:

```python
def is_optimistic_candidate_block(opt_store, current_slot, block) -> bool:
    if is_execution_block(opt_store.blocks[block.parent_root]):   # parent.body.execution_payload != empty
        return True
    if block.slot + SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY <= current_slot:
        return True
    return False
```

and its "Checkpoint Sync" section lets the anchor be assumed `VALID`.
ethlambda reads `is_execution_block(parent)` off the execution-hash
cache, which was filled only when a block was imported. The anchor is
never imported, so its first child looked like the child of a pre-merge
block. The same gap made `forkchoiceUpdated` send a zero finalized/safe
hash for the anchor, and a restart emptied the cache for every stored
block (embedded ethrex restarts a few dozen blocks behind and answers
`SYNCING`, so the park could repeat after a restart).

## What Changed

- `SignedBeaconBlock::execution_block_hash_if_execution_block` (types):
the one rule for which blocks have an execution hash to cache (the
payload hash, minus a pre-merge all-zero one). Import now uses it, with
no behavior change.
- `get_forkchoice_store`: caches the anchor's payload hash. Only the
hash, no verdict.
- `Store::restore_beacon_scratch`: on resume, rebuilds the cache for the
unfinalized `LiveChain` window it already walks, against each block's
own slot so pruning still bounds it.
- `docs/beacon_engine.md` and the doc comments: the cache is filled at
import, for the anchor, and on resume. The section that described the
anchor park as expected behavior now describes the fix.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Nothing is marked validated: the anchor and resumed blocks get their
hash only, so `optimistic_roots`, payload verdicts and `latestValidHash`
handling are unchanged.
- Pre-merge bellatrix blocks (zero payload hash), phase0/altair and
gloas blocks still cache nothing, so the 128-slot horizon still guards
the merge transition and gloas is untouched.
- Behavior change: after checkpoint sync or a restart, the first new
block is an optimistic candidate at once; fcU's finalized/safe hash is
the anchor's payload hash instead of zero.

## Tests Added / Run

- `execution_block_hash_if_execution_block_gives_post_merge_hashes_only`
(types)
- `a_post_merge_anchor_makes_its_first_child_an_optimistic_candidate`,
`an_anchor_with_no_execution_payload_caches_no_hash`, plus a
gloas-anchor assertion (fork choice)
- `resume_rebuilds_execution_hashes_for_the_unfinalized_window`
(storage)
- `cargo test --profile release-fast --lib` for `ethlambda-types`,
`ethlambda-storage`, `ethlambda-state-transition`,
`ethlambda-blockchain`: all pass.
- Live, on ethrex's multisync (ethrex+ethlambda on Hoodi, Sepolia and
Platåberget) with an image of this branch: three full runs passed every
EL and CL check on all three pairs, with no `not an optimistic
candidate` line in any Hoodi log. Hoodi synced in 24 to 29 minutes.
Before the fix, Hoodi failed its first run with the head stuck at the
anchor for 10 minutes.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to lambdaclass/ethrex#7461 (the multisync check that found it)

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — only the four crates' `--lib` tests above were run

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(beacon): check vote signatures under the fork schedule's domain (#673)
body:
## Problem

Gossip and the Beacon API verify vote signatures against a state that
was never advanced to the vote's epoch:

| Path | State used |
|---|---|
| `beacon_attestation_{subnet}` gossip
(`gossip::attestation::stateful_checks`) | voted block's post-state |
| `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` gossip and `POST
/eth/v2/validator/aggregate_and_proofs`
(`gossip::aggregate::stateful_checks`) | voted block's post-state |
| `POST /eth/v2/beacon/pool/attestations` (`pool::validate`) | head's
post-state |

`get_domain` takes the fork version from `state.fork`. If a fork's first
slots are empty, that state is still the previous fork's, so a correctly
signed vote of the new fork fails its signature check. Gossip REJECTs
it, which also penalizes the peer that relayed it, and a validator
client gets "invalid signature". This lasts until a block of the new
fork is imported.

Seen on a fulu-to-gloas transition devnet:
- With slots 160 and 161 (the first two gloas slots) empty, every
ethlambda node refused every client's attestations for them.
- A node whose head stayed pre-fork through an execution-client outage
refused all of the fork's first epoch.

## Fix

- `get_domain_from_schedule(config, state, domain_type, epoch)` reads
the fork version from the config's schedule at `epoch`. It is used for:
  - the subnet attestation signature;
- the aggregate's selection proof, its aggregator signature and the
aggregate signature itself;
  - the pool endpoint.
- `is_valid_indexed_attestation_with_domain` (phase0 and electra) is the
existing check with the domain passed in. `is_valid_indexed_attestation`
is now a thin wrapper over it, so the state transition is unchanged.
- The state transition keeps `get_domain`, since it advances the state
to the slot first and there the two agree. Operation gossip (slashings)
keeps it too, since the spec checks those against the head state as-is.

## Tests

- `the_schedule_names_the_new_fork_before_the_state_reaches_it`: the two
readings agree on the old fork's epochs and differ at the new fork's
first.
- `a_vote_across_a_fork_boundary_verifies_under_the_new_forks_version`
(gossip), `an_attestation_in_a_forks_first_empty_slot_is_published` and
`an_aggregate_in_a_forks_first_empty_slot_is_published` (API): an
electra head, a fulu vote. Each fails without the fix: `BadSignature`,
or a 400.
- The rpc tests now sign votes under the schedule, as a validator client
does, rather than under the test states' all-zero `fork`.

`cargo test --workspace --profile release-fast --lib --bins` passes, as
do the 96 gossip spec vectors (`--features beacon-spec-tests --
gossip/`) and `make lint`.

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: chore: drop the kurtosis-validator wrapper in favor of our ethereum-package fork (#690)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`tooling/kurtosis-validator` wrapped upstream ethereum-package to bolt
one ethlambda validator client (and optionally an `ethlambda beacon`)
onto a finished devnet. Our fork,
[`lambdaclass/ethereum-package@add-ethlambda`](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethereum-package/tree/add-ethlambda),
now adds ethlambda as a native `cl_type` and `vc_type`, so the wrapper
is redundant:

- ethlambda participants are ordinary ethereum-package services, so the
package's own additional services (assertoor, dora) see them. The
wrapper's services were invisible to them.
- The wrapper imported `github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package`
unpinned, and its `kurtosis.yml` still named `ethlambda_private`.

## What Changed

- Deleted `tooling/kurtosis-validator/` (`main.star`, `kurtosis.yml`,
three `network_params*.yaml`).
- `docs/rpc.md`: the one reference to it now points at the fork.

## Scenario mapping

| Wrapper args file | Fork equivalent |
|---|---|
| `network_params.yaml` (ethlambda VC on lighthouse BN) | `cl_type:
lighthouse`, `vc_type: ethlambda` |
| `network_params_ethlambda_beacon.yaml` (ethlambda VC on ethlambda
beacon) | `cl_type: ethlambda` (VC defaults to ethlambda) |
| `network_params_lighthouse_vc.yaml` (Lighthouse VC + doppelganger on
ethlambda beacon) | `cl_type: ethlambda`, `vc_type: lighthouse`,
`vc_extra_params: [--enable-doppelganger-protection]` (accepted by the
fork's input parser; not run) |

The fork refuses `cl_type: ethlambda` as the first participant unless
bootnodoor is enabled, since ethlambda reports no ENR over the Beacon
API. See the fork's `.github/tests/ethlambda.yaml` for a working
example.

One note from the deleted yaml comments is not encoded in the fork:
lighthouse peers with few validators of their own want
`--subscribe-all-subnets` (`cl_extra_params`), because ethlambda beacon
publishes attestations through gossipsub fanout, which reaches only
peers subscribed to the subnet. (The other note, lighthouse's
`--target-peers=0` pin, no longer applies: ethereum-package adds it only
when lighthouse is the sole participant.)

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

No code or CI change; nothing in the workspace, Makefile or workflows
referenced the wrapper.

## Tests Added / Run

None: no Rust touched. `git grep kurtosis-validator` is empty after the
change.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to #679 (kurtosis + assertoor battery, which runs on the fork)

subject: feat(beacon): log a Glamsterdam banner after the first gloas block (#666)
body:
## Summary

Logs a Glamsterdam banner when the fork actually goes live, following
lambdaclass/ethrex#7341:

- **Trigger:** the import of the chain's first gloas block, meaning the
first block gloas applies to while it did not apply to its parent.
Missed slots at the start of the fork epoch still leave a first block.
It fires on every import route (gossip, range sync, a block this node's
validator client published), right after the block's own `Block imported
successfully` line.
- **Once per process:** the decision settles on the first gloas block
the process imports, banner or not. Blocks import parent-first, so a
node that sees the chain's first gloas block sees it before any other
gloas block. A node started or checkpoint-synced after the fork logs
nothing, and it does not pay a whole-block parent decode on every later
import to learn that again.

wordmark and Glamsterdam's, in

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: feat(storage): count state cache hits and misses (#659)
body:
Stacked on #658: `has_state` only consults the state cache from that PR
on.

## Motivation

Nothing reports whether a state lookup was served from `Store`'s
32-entry state LRU. Two slow paths seen on the followers can only be
blamed on cache misses by inference today:

- the epoch-boundary head recompute (0.5-4 s), where
`checkpoint_state(E-1, R)` likely misses and rebuilds the state on the
chain actor
- import guards, where a `has_state` that misses the cache falls through
to RocksDB

## Change

One counter, `lean_state_cache_lookups_total{method, kind, result}`:

| label | values | why |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `get_state`, `has_state`, `cached_state` | gossip
validation calls `cached_state` once per attestation and aggregate;
summed, it would bury the import path's misses |
| `kind` | `block`, `checkpoint` | a checkpoint-state miss is the one
the epoch-tick head recompute pays |
| `result` | `hit`, `miss` | |

Where each lookup is counted:

| site | `method` | LRU op |
|---|---|---|
| `read_state` (behind `get_state`, and the writer thread's lean parent
read) | `get_state` | `get` |
| `Store::cached_state` (fork choice's `checkpoint_state`, gossip
validation, head state) | `cached_state` | `get` |
| `Store::has_state` | `has_state` | `peek` |

`read_state` and `cached_state` share a new `state_writer::cache_get`
helper, so the counting lives in one place. `rebase_onto_resident`'s
peek is not counted: it picks a base to share memory with, not the state
being asked for.

### Behavior change: `has_state` checks the cache before
`pending_states`

This is the same order `read_state` uses. A state in flight is in both,
so no answer changes. With `pending_states` first, a just-imported
parent was answered before the cache check and its lookup went
uncounted.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p ethlambda-storage --profile release-fast --lib`: 146
passed
- `cargo clippy -p ethlambda-storage --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
clean
- One-off local check (not committed) that each of `cached_state` hit
(block), `cached_state` miss (checkpoint), `has_state` hit/miss and
`get_state` hit/miss increments exactly its own series once. Not
committed because the counter lives in the global registry, which every
test in the crate shares, so an exact-count assertion would be racy
under parallel tests.
- Spec suites not run locally.

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: docs: describe ethlambda as a Beacon Chain and Lean Chain client (#715)
body:
## Motivation

The project's self-descriptions still called ethlambda a Lean consensus
client only, and `CLAUDE.md` said it was "not to be confused with" a
Beacon Chain client. Since `ethlambda beacon` follows the Beacon Chain,
those statements are wrong.

## Changes

Every place that describes what ethlambda is now says "Beacon Chain and
Lean Chain client":

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Tagline; "Current status" now names both chains (beacon
side points at the follower quickstart) and scopes the existing bullet
list to the Lean Chain |
| `book.toml`, `docs/introduction.md` | Book description and intro. The
intro also gains the **Beacon Chain** part that `SUMMARY.md` already
lists ("four parts" was five) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `Dockerfile` (image label),
`.github/prompts/ai-review.md` | One-line descriptions |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Replaces "not to be confused with Beacon Chain clients"
with the two sub-commands |
| `docs/infographics/*.html` | Subtitle and footer only |
| `docs/lmd_ghost.md` | The comparison table and paragraphs credited
"ethlambda" with having no proposer boost or equivocation discounting;
that is only true of the Lean Chain, since the beacon fork choice
implements both. Scoped to the Lean Chain |

Pages that spoke of "ethlambda" or "the node" while meaning the Lean
Chain alone now say so. The Lean content itself is unchanged:

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `docs/3sf_mini.md`, `docs/lmd_ghost.md`, `docs/slots_and_intervals.md`
| The "In ethlambda" notes become "In ethlambda's Lean Chain" (one said
every validator has equal weight, which beacon does not do). The
3SF-mini and LMD-GHOST intros name `ethlambda node`, and LMD-GHOST
points at the beacon fork choice |
| `docs/architecture.md` | A scope note: the page describes `ethlambda
node`; `ethlambda beacon` runs the same two actors without keys,
aggregation or duties |
| `docs/benchmarking.md` | `synthetic` is Lean Chain block building,
`import` is Beacon Chain block import |
| `docs/metrics.md` | leanMetrics applies to the Lean Chain; points at
where the beacon metrics are |
| `docs/fork_choice_visualization.md` | Served by `ethlambda node` only
(`/lean/v0` is a 404 on beacon) |
| `docs/introduction.md` | Spec deviations cover consensus-specs too |
| `README.md` | The `node` section no longer claims the rest of the
README is about it |

Left as is, since they already describe the Lean side specifically:
`docs/cli.md`, `docs/checkpoint_sync.md`, `docs/beacon_stf.md`, the
README's per-sub-command headers, `.claude/skills/*`, and code comments.

## Open questions

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` still says "Lean Consensus is a clean slate. Don't
add backward compatibility for deprecated features." The beacon side
carries phase0 through gloas by necessity. Should that bullet be scoped
to the Lean Chain?
- The architecture infographic's body is all Lean (3SF-mini badge, lean
actors); only its subtitle changed here.
- The README roadmap still lists execution client integration as future
work.

subject: docs: document the release binary, the validator client and the beacon node's duties (#716)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
- Ahead of 1.0, the README still describes a Lean-only client whose
beacon quickstart runs from a hand-published Docker tag. The release
ships a Beacon Chain node that serves a validator client, the validator
client itself, and binaries for three platforms, none of which the
README shows how to run.

corrects statements that no longer hold.

## What Changed
`README.md` only:

binary**: download the asset, generate the node key, run `ethlambda
beacon` with no execution client, with the AVX2 and glibc requirements,
the macOS quarantine note, the provenance-verification pointer, and
`KillSignal=SIGINT` for systemd (the node shuts down gracefully on

an execution client, joining the subnets its validators ask for and
publishing what they sign. The old text said it publishes nothing and
joins no subnet.
- Platåberget paragraph: the validator endpoints serve gloas duties. The
old text said they refuse a gloas epoch.
- Roadmap: the state-diffs item is removed as shipped (#238 is closed);

author: Pablo Deymonnaz
subject: chore(deps): bump quinn-proto, h2, rkyv and crossbeam-epoch past RustSec advisories (#718)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`cargo audit` against `main` reports 23 advisories. One of them can be
triggered remotely by any peer: `quinn-proto` 0.11.14, the QUIC
implementation behind libp2p-quic, our primary transport, is open to
remote memory exhaustion from unbounded out-of-order stream reassembly
([RUSTSEC-2026-0185](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0185),
CVSS 7.5) and to unbounded growth of pending connection-ID retirements
([RUSTSEC-2026-0339](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0339)).
Both need no authentication.

This PR takes every fix that already clears the 14-day publish-age
cooldown and needs nothing but a lockfile change.

## What Changed

`Cargo.lock` only, via `make update UPDATE_ARGS="-p quinn-proto -p h2 -p
rkyv -p crossbeam-epoch"` (so the cooldown is applied):

| Crate | From → to | Advisories fixed | Reachable here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quinn-proto` | 0.11.14 → 0.11.19 | 0185, 0339 (and 0338, 0340, 0342)
| **Yes**: 0185 and 0339 from any QUIC peer. 0342 is not (libp2p-quic
disables datagrams), nor are 0340/0338 (ACK_FREQUENCY not enabled, no
unordered reads) |
| `h2` | 0.4.14 → 0.4.20 | 0258 (unbounded empty DATA frames) | Client
side only (reqwest); our axum servers are HTTP/1 only |
| `rkyv` / `rkyv_derive` | 0.8.16 → 0.8.18 | 0233, 0234, 0235 | No:
pulled in by ethrex-common, which we never feed peer-supplied archives |
| `crossbeam-epoch` | 0.9.18 → 0.9.21 | 0204 (`fmt::Pointer` on an
invalid pointer) | No |

`quinn-proto` 0.11.19 adds one new transitive dependency, `rand_pcg`
0.10.2.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- No source changes, and no change to any direct dependency's
requirement in a `Cargo.toml`.
- Every new version is semver-compatible with the one it replaces and
older than the cooldown; `make cooldown-check` passes.

### Deliberately left out

| Crate | Why not here |
|---|---|
| `rustls` (0285, 0346, 0348, 0349), `rustls-webpki` (0382),
`webpki-roots` (0381) | The fixed `rustls` (≥ 0.23.45) needs
`rustls-webpki` 0.103.16, published 2026-10-20, which is still inside
the cooldown: the resolver stops at `rustls` 0.23.43, which fixes none
of them. A follow-up after 2026-11-03 picks all three up together. |
| `crypto-bigint` 0.5.5 (0387) | Fixed only in 0.7, which needs an
upstream `elliptic-curve`/`k256` major bump. |
| `ruint` 1.18.0 (0220) | Reached through leanVM's `xmss` →
`ethereum_ssz`; the fix pulls in `ark-ff` 0.6, so it belongs with a
leanVM bump. |
| `hickory-proto` (0118, 0119), `quick-xml` (0194, 0195), `zstd-sys`
(0410) | Not reachable: libp2p's DNS/mDNS transports are compiled
(`full`) but unused, `quick-xml` only serves `inferno`'s SVG output
under `jemalloc_pprof`, and the `zstd-sys` issue is wasm-only. |

After this PR `cargo audit` reports 13 advisories, none of them in
`quinn-proto`, `h2`, `rkyv` or `crossbeam-epoch`.

## Tests Added / Run

None added: no source touched.

- `make cooldown-check`: passes
- `make lint`: clean
- `make test`: 2859 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo audit`: 23 → 13 advisories

## Related Issues / PRs

- Follow-up: `rustls` / `rustls-webpki` / `webpki-roots` once
`rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 clears the cooldown (2026-11-03).

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [x] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — all passing

author: Pablo Deymonnaz
subject: fix: cap gossipsub's log output at ERROR unless RUST_LOG raises it (#719)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
- A beacon node on Hoodi logs `WARN libp2p_gossipsub::behaviour: Send
Queue full. Could not send Rpc.` once per heartbeat for every slow peer,
each line listing every IHAVE id dropped on an attestation subnet. The
drop is already counted in the peer's `failed_messages` and charged to
its score, so the line adds noise, not information.
- The line is emitted inside the gossipsub crate. Rather than patching
the libp2p fork, the node's default log filter now caps that crate at
ERROR, which is how an operator sees the dependency's noise anyway.
Lighthouse goes further and routes all `libp2p_gossipsub` and `discv5`
output to separate files.

## What Changed
- `bin/ethlambda/src/main.rs`: `init_node_logging` builds its filter
from `node_log_filter(RUST_LOG)`. With no `RUST_LOG` the directives are
`info,libp2p_gossipsub=error`; with one they are
`libp2p_gossipsub=error,<RUST_LOG>`. A `RUST_LOG` directive on
`libp2p_gossipsub` replaces the cap, one on any other target adds to it,
and `RUST_LOG` keeps replacing the `info` floor the way `from_env_lossy`
always did. The floor is spelled out because `EnvFilter` only applies a
default directive when it was given no directive at all.
- Besides the send-queue line, the cap hides gossipsub's other warnings
(bad signatures, substream limits, anonymous-mode field checks), all
per-peer protocol violations that peer scoring already handles. Its 19
error sites still show.
- The benchmark and keygen filters are untouched; neither runs a
network.
- `docs/beacon_wire.md`: one sentence next to the existing `RUST_LOG`
example, saying how to see gossipsub's warnings.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees
- Default output changes only for the `libp2p_gossipsub` target: WARN
and below are dropped, ERROR stays.
- `RUST_LOG` semantics are preserved, including the pre-existing quirk
that a `RUST_LOG` without its own `info` silences other targets.
Verified against tracing-subscriber 0.3.23: an equal-specificity
directive added later replaces the earlier one, and `Ordering::Equal`
implies the same target, so no other directive is clobbered.
- A bare `RUST_LOG=debug` keeps the cap, since the more specific
directive wins; the doc comment says to name the crate.

## Tests Added / Run
- Three tests in `main.rs` drive real events through the filter: default
behaviour (INFO floor, gossipsub WARN dropped, gossipsub ERROR kept),
the lift via `RUST_LOG=…,libp2p_gossipsub=warn,…` alongside another
directive, and the floor-replacement quirk.
- `cargo test --locked --profile release-fast -p ethlambda --bin
ethlambda -- tests::node_logging tests::rust_log`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p ethlambda --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Related Issues / PRs
- Supersedes #717 and lambdaclass/rust-libp2p#1, which fixed the same
symptom in the fork; both are being closed.
- Follow-up worth an issue: ethlambda does not handle gossipsub's
`Event::SlowPeer`. Lighthouse reports a peer after more than 10 priority
or 10 non-priority drops, so the peer producing these lines gets
disconnected instead of staying in the mesh.

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [ ] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — run as `cargo clippy
-p ethlambda --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the only crate changed; CI
runs the workspace
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — the three new tests run at `release-fast`; CI runs the
rest

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix: v1.0.0 release feedback (docker stop, version note, shutdown log, identity metadata, anchor canonical) (#727)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Fixes from testing the v1.0.0 release (`ethlambda beacon` on mainnet,
Docker and the release binary). Four commits, one per finding:

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| `docker stop` force-kills after 10 s, but a clean shutdown during
catch-up took 14.3 s, so the state was lost | README: `--stop-timeout
60` on both `docker run` lines |
| The release binary's `--version` says `-rc.2-` while the image says
`-stable-`, and only RELEASE.md explains why | README: one note next to
the binary instructions, linking RELEASE.md#version-string (the release
notes link this README) |
| Every clean Ctrl+C logged `ERROR ... P2P networking is no longer
functional` | The swarm loop's exit is logged at info when the P2P actor
shut down; error only when the swarm itself ends |
| `/eth/v1/node/identity` `metadata` was a placeholder (seq 0, no
subnets), disagreeing with the ENR's `attnets` | The endpoint reports
the live `MetaData` peers get over req/resp |
| `/eth/v1/beacon/headers/head` returned `canonical: false` while the
head was still the checkpoint anchor | The beacon bootstrap indexes the
anchor's slot in `BlockRoots`, as lean's `init_store` already does |

Not fixed here: `is_syncing` and `/eth/v1/node/health` misreport during
catch-up (health `200` while 80+ slots behind). The cause is that the
beacon sync tracker's "freshest block seen" counts only imported blocks,
so pending gossip blocks during catch-up look like a network stall.
Changing that input has a security trade-off (leanSpec counts only
signature-valid blocks so a peer cannot fake freshness), so this PR only
widens the README caveat.

## What Changed

- **README.md**: `--stop-timeout 60`, the version-string note, and a
wider `is_syncing`/health caveat.
- **`crates/net/p2p/src/swarm_adapter.rs`**: `swarm_loop` breaks with a
`LoopExit` reason. A channel closed by the P2P actor is a graceful
shutdown (`info`). An actor panic looks the same from here, but
spawned-concurrency logs it as an error before stopping the actor.
- **Identity `MetaData`**:
- `ethlambda-network-api` gains
`MetaDataController`/`AdvertisedMetaData`, a shared handle in the
`SyncStatusController` mould.
- `BeaconWire` publishes to it at startup and on every sequence-number
bump, all of which now go through `BeaconWire::bump_metadata_seq_number`
(fork digest switch, sync committee subnet join and leave).
- `P2P::local_metadata()` hands it to `main.rs`, which puts it in
`BeaconIdentity`; `get_identity` reads it per request.
- **Anchor index**:
- `Store::index_beacon_anchor` writes the anchor's `BlockRoots` row,
keyed by the anchor **block's** slot (a checkpoint state sits after its
latest block when the epoch's first slot was empty).
- `get_forkchoice_store` calls it right after inserting the anchor
block, and so does the RPC test fixture that mirrors it.
- Docs in `block_id.rs`, `docs/data_storage.md` and `docs/rpc.md`
updated.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- `metadata.seq_number` is the MetaData counter, not the ENR's `seq`:
the p2p specification counts the two separately, so they can still
differ. `attnets` now matches the ENR.
- With the anchor indexed, `BeaconBlocksByRange` serves the anchor block
too (BlocksByRoot already did). Its data columns were never fetched, so
a columns-by-range answer still has none for that slot.
- Directories bootstrapped before this change have no anchor row. Slot
lookups there keep falling back to `anchored_root_at_slot` (the head,
justified and finalized roots). No `DB_VERSION` bump.
- Lean is unaffected: the anchor index is beacon-only and lean has no
`MetaData`.

## Tests Added / Run

- `canonical_is_checked_against_the_index` now expects the anchor to be
`true` (it pinned the old gap) and adds a non-canonical sibling that
must be `false`.
- New: `index_beacon_anchor_keys_the_row_by_the_blocks_slot` (storage),
`the_beacon_api_copy_follows_every_change` (p2p),
`identity_reports_the_metadata_peers_are_told` (rpc).
- `cargo test --profile release-fast --lib` for `ethlambda-storage`,
`-rpc`, `-p2p`, `-network-api`, `-state-transition`, `-blockchain`: all
pass. leanSpec fixture tests not run.

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — only the `--lib` targets above

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(p2p): wait out the peers' backoff before regrafting a left topic (#728)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

On a 7-node all-ethlambda kurtosis devnet (`ethlambda-all.yaml` from our
ethereum-package fork, image 1.0.0), every CL logged this at the start
of epoch 5, against the same two peers:

```
WARN libp2p_gossipsub::behaviour: [Penalty] Peer attempted graft within backoff time, penalizing peer=...
```

The two penalized nodes had each left an attestation subnet when an
aggregator duty expired at the end of epoch 4. At the epoch 5 boundary,
the VC's duties for epoch 6 asked for that subnet again, and the node
rejoined about 23 s (and, on the other node, 55 s) after leaving. The
trigger is a duty on a subnet in the last slots of epoch N, none in N+1,
and one in N+2.

The cause is an asymmetry in rust-libp2p gossipsub (verified at our
pinned rev `2f14d0e`):

| Side | What it does | Backoff |
|---|---|---|
| Leaver | Sends UNSUBSCRIBE, then PRUNE carrying `unsubscribe_backoff`;
won't graft for that long | 10 s default |
| Receiver | Handling the UNSUBSCRIBE, removes the peer from the mesh
with `remove_peer_from_mesh(.., None, ..)`; `None` means
`prune_backoff`. Backoffs are only ever extended, so the PRUNE's shorter
value can't shorten it | 60 s default |

So the leaver regrafts after 10 s into peers still holding a 60 s
backoff. They reject the graft and add a behaviour penalty (P7).

## What Changed

- `crates/net/p2p/src/lib.rs`: a `PRUNE_BACKOFF` constant (60 s,
gossipsub's default) set as both `prune_backoff` and
`unsubscribe_backoff` in `gossipsub_config`, so this node waits as long
after leaving a topic as its peers do. Plus a unit test checking that
the unsubscribe backoff is at least a default peer's prune backoff.
- `docs/beacon_wire.md`: a third "difference from lighthouse" bullet in
Peer scoring explaining the choice.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- The mesh on a rejoined subnet comes back no later than before. The
early grafts were rejected anyway, so the subnet's mesh was empty for
the peers' 60 s either way; this only stops the node from being
penalized for trying.
- No effect on lean: its subscriptions are fixed at startup and never
left.
- Severity was low. One penalty per peer per event, and the behaviour
penalty only counts past its threshold, so it would take about 10 such
events per epoch, sustained, to reach the gossip threshold. Lighthouse
would penalize us the same way, since it uses the same rust-libp2p
defaults.

**What the specs say**

- consensus-specs (`v1.7.0-beta.2`, `phase0/p2p-interface.md`) fixes
`D`, `D_low`, `D_high`, `D_lazy`, the heartbeat, `fanout_ttl`,
`mcache_*` and `seen_ttl`, and leaves gossipsub v1.1's extra parameters
(backoffs, scoring) "under investigation". For subnets, it asks for
`SUBNETS_PER_NODE` long-lived subscriptions held for
`EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs. An aggregator joins its duty's
subnet (`phase0/validator.md`), but nothing says how long to stay.
- The libp2p gossipsub v1.1 spec recommends a 1-minute `PruneBackoff`
and a 10 s `UnsubscribeBackoff`, and expects the leaver's PRUNE to carry
the shorter one. rust-libp2p's receiver doesn't honor it, which is the
asymmetry above.
- Lighthouse sets neither backoff, and unsubscribes 2 slots after an
aggregator duty (`UNSUBSCRIBE_AFTER_AGGREGATOR_DUTY`).

An alternative is to keep an expired aggregator subnet until the next
epoch's duty refresh, so the leave never happens in the first place. I
didn't take it because it changes subscription logic rather than one
parameter, and still leaves other leave-and-rejoin paths exposed.

## Tests Added / Run

- `rejoining_a_topic_waits_out_the_backoff_peers_apply_to_a_leaver`
(new)
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-p2p --lib --profile release-fast`: 361
passed, 1 ignored (an existing devnet3 fixture)
- `make fmt`, `make lint`

## Related Issues / PRs

- Found while running lambdaclass/ethereum-package's
`ethlambda-all.yaml` after lambdaclass/ethereum-package@1b7aa4d6, which
lets an ethlambda CL be the bootnode.

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — all passing (not run: only `ethlambda-p2p`'s lib tests
above)

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: docs(release): document the Homebrew formula bump (#723)
body:
## Motivation

ethlambda is getting a Homebrew formula in `lambdaclass/homebrew-tap`
(lambdaclass/homebrew-tap#31), so cutting a release now includes
pointing that formula at it. RELEASE.md still listed Homebrew as future
work.

## Description

- New step 6 in "Cutting a release": the manual formula bump, modeled on
ethrex's. It hashes the final tag's source tarball, repackages
`ethlambda-macos-aarch64` as the `arm64_sonoma` bottle (with
`--no-xattrs --no-mac-metadata`, so macOS provenance attributes stay out
of the archive), attaches it to an `ethlambda-vX.Y.Z` tap release, and
opens the formula PR. "Merge the release branch" becomes step 7.
- "Distribution channels" and the intro now list the tap; apt stays
future work.

The tap release is tagged `ethlambda-vX.Y.Z` because the tap's bare
`vX.Y.Z` tags are ethrex's, and it is created with `--latest=false` so
ethrex's release stays the tap's latest.

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(blockchain): stop the missing-ancestor walk at an imported block (#720)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

An `ethlambda beacon` (v1.0.0-rc.2) paired with geth v1.17.10 on Hoodi
stopped importing at slot 4248640 and stayed there for three hours.
Found by ethrex's multisync (lambdaclass/ethrex#7461): the pair failed
its 10-minute head-stall check while the same image passed with
nethermind and ethrex.

The trigger was geth: mid snap sync, it answered `engine_newPayloadV4`
past the 8 s engine ladder, so block 4248641 got no verdict and was
dropped, as designed (`ImportOutcome::Held`). What should retry such a
block is the next arrival: `process_or_pend_block` resolves the
arrival's missing ancestor through `pending_block_parents`, and the DB
walk then re-queues the first stored block whose parent has a state.

That resolution is what went wrong. `pending_block_parents` stores the
missing ancestor as it was when each block pended. Every descendant of
4248641 had pended while 4248639 was the gap, so all of them pointed at
4248639. Once 4248639 imported and 4248641 was dropped after it, every
arrival resolved to 4248639. The DB walk re-queued that already-imported
block (a no-op through the "already in the store" early return) and
returned before `request_missing_block`, so 4248641 was never retried or
requested, and ~900 later blocks stayed parked. Only a re-delivery of
4248642, whose parent is 4248641 itself, could have recovered it, and
none came.

The same run's Sepolia pair dropped 11 blocks for lack of a verdict and
recovered every time, because its pointers happened to land on the
dropped block.

## What Changed

- `process_or_pend_block` (`crates/blockchain/src/lib.rs`): the
`pending_block_parents` walk stops at an ancestor that already has a
post-state. The existing DB walk then steps through the gap block by
block, finds the dropped block, re-queues it, and re-points each pending
block it passes at its direct parent.
- `ImportOutcome::Held` doc: a no-verdict block is re-driven by the next
arrival that leads to it (from the DB, or by asking the network), not by
a timer.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- A walk that never meets an imported ancestor behaves exactly as
before.
- Cost: one `has_state` read per pointer step. Normally that is one
step, since pointers jump straight to the top of a gap; while a gap
opened this way is still open, later arrivals step through it a block at
a time.
- Not changed: a no-verdict block is still dropped, and only an arrival
that leads to it retries it. Nothing retries it on a timer.
- The code path is chain-agnostic, so lean gets the same guard.

## Tests Added / Run

-
`a_block_dropped_below_an_imported_ancestor_is_retried_by_the_next_arrival`:
an imported ancestor, its child dropped with no state, a grandchild
still pointing at the ancestor, then one arrival. Asserts the dropped
block is what gets queued. Without the guard it fails, queueing the
imported ancestor instead.
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-blockchain --lib --profile release-fast`: 292
passed, 43 ignored.
- Not yet verified live.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to lambdaclass/ethrex#7461 (the multisync check that found it)

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at
`release-fast`) — only `ethlambda-blockchain --lib` was run

author: Tomás Grüner
subject: fix(metrics): serve the process collector's memory and CPU metrics (#750)
body:
The beacon dashboard's "Resident memory" panel reads
`process_resident_memory_bytes{job="beacon"}`, which no ethlambda build
exported. The `prometheus` crate only registers its process collector
with the default registry when its `process` feature is on. Only the
embedded-ethrex follower had it, because ethrex turns the feature on and
features unify. Every other node's memory panel was blank, eth-2, eth-3
and eth-4 included.

### What changed

- `Cargo.toml`: `prometheus = { version = "0.14", features = ["process"]
}`. On Linux the default registry, which `/metrics` gathers from
(`gather_default_metrics`), now carries `process_resident_memory_bytes`,
`process_virtual_memory_bytes`, `process_cpu_seconds_total`,
`process_open_fds`, `process_max_fds`, `process_threads` and
`process_start_time_seconds`, read from `/proc/self` at each scrape.
Other platforms are unchanged.
- `Cargo.lock`: adds `procfs`/`procfs-core` 0.17.0, plus the older
`rustix` 0.38 and `linux-raw-sys` 0.4 they depend on. `make
cooldown-check` passes.
- `docs/metrics.md`: the process metrics, under Node Info Metrics.
- A Linux-only unit test that the default registry serves
`process_resident_memory_bytes`, so dropping the feature fails CI
instead of blanking the dashboard.

### Tests

- `make lint` clean, `make cooldown-check` passes (macOS; the new test
is compiled out there).
